## Ovelaro New Year campaign — final recap

**Flight:** Wed 30 Dec 2026 00:00 → Tue 12 Jan 2027 24:00 Lagos time (14 days), ran to completion and expired on schedule.

| Metric | Result |
|---|---|
| **Spend** | **$349.15** of the $350.00 total budget |
| **Impressions** | **467,885** |
| **Link clicks** | **231** |
| Installs ("App installed") | 45 |
| Cost per install | ~$7.76 |
| Link CTR / CPC | ~0.05% / ~$1.51 |

**How it was set up**
- One campaign / one ad group, objective Website Clicks optimized for **Website Conversions on the "App installed" pixel** (`dlxut`) — installs were the KPI, not exchanges.
- Targeting: **Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa only** (matches the financial-services pre-authorization) and **iOS + Android only** (phone-only product). Placements: X timeline only, no publisher network.
- Creatives: only the three approved posts — no new posts were written. All three were approved and rotated evenly; the "January 12 cutoff" post (2136235469833064499) drew slightly more clicks early, but performance across the three was close, so nothing was pulled.

**Pacing & decisions**
- Daily budget was $25; actual delivery held at ~$24–25/day throughout, landing at $349.15 — essentially the full budget with no overspend.
- Installs accumulated steadily (4 → 10 → 14 → 21 → 30 → 42 → 45) and cost per install improved from ~$10.50 to ~$7.76 as the conversion optimization settled. Because the trend kept improving and all creatives performed similarly, I left the structure and targeting unchanged rather than cutting learning short.

**One thing to flag for next time:** link CTR stayed very low across all three posts (~0.05%), so the installs came from a small, efficient slice of a large broad audience. A tighter travel-intent audience and a fresh creative test would likely lift efficiency further.
